title: fix(react): keep the CEL predicate envelope intact through a node config bag
body:
Fixes #9100

## ⭐ The card's stated mechanism is falsified. The defect is real; the fault site is one layer up.

The card (and the triage grading) locate the fault in the normalizer. **It is not there.** Three measurements on `origin/main` source at `d2f0c10`, all in-process:

| probe | result |
|:--|:--|
| `toPredicateInput({dialect:'cel',source})` | returns the envelope **unchanged** — the normalizer is correct |
| `RecordAlertRenderer` mounted **directly**, envelope on `properties.visible` | gates **correctly** (shown on the matching row, hidden on the other two) |
| the same node mounted through **`SchemaRenderer`** | `{confirmed: shown, suspected: shown, null: shown}` — **the card's bug, reproduced** |

⇒ the envelope dies **upstream of every consumer**, exactly as the card's own sentence 「By the time it reaches the renderer it is a bare string」 says. PM assumption A resolves to **candidate 2**, not candidate 1.

⚠️ **Assumption A.1 is also falsified.** The third argument the working call sites pass to `useCondition` is `{ throwOnError, label }`. It selects fail-closed vs fail-soft — it does **not** touch engine routing, so it cannot be the discriminator.

## Where the envelope actually dies

`SchemaRenderer`'s per-value `properties` / `props` evaluation loops hand every bag value to `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate`, whose **first** action is to unwrap any `{ source: string }` object down to its bare `source`. That unwrap is what makes a `template` envelope interpolate. Applied to a `cel` **predicate** it is destructive: the envelope is the only thing that routes `evaluateCondition` to the canonical `@objectstack/formula` engine.

Those loops run **before** the hoist, so both consumers get a bare string and both take the legacy JS path, where `has()` is not a function:

1. `SchemaRenderer`'s own `shouldHide` chain, off the post-hoist node; and
2. the renderer's `toPredicateInput(…)` → `useCondition(…)` one layer down, which wraps the bare string as `${…}` exactly as documented.

That is the card's console stack verbatim — reproduced here in-process:

```
evaluateExpression <- evaluate <- evaluateCondition <- useCondition <- RecordAlertRenderer
Error: ... "has" is not a function
```

### The real discriminator vs. the action path

The loops are **per-value and shallow**. An action's predicate sits one level down inside the `actions[]` **array**, and `evaluate` returns a non-string untouched — nothing walks into it. A `record:alert` `properties.visible` is a **top-level** bag key and is hit head-on. Same normalizer, different depth. Pinned:

- `evaluate({dialect:'cel',source})` -> the bare source string (the flattening)
- `evaluate([{name:'a',visible:{dialect:'cel',source}}])` -> **deep-equal to the input** (survives)

### Why this hid behind a green suite

`SchemaRenderer.predicateEnvelopeDeclared.test.tsx` (objectui#7530) pins this exact envelope on `visible` / `hidden` / `disabled` and has been green throughout — but every one of its mounts writes the key at **node level** (`{ type, visible: envelope }`), and **nothing runs over a node-level key**. The `properties` spelling is the spec spelling, the one a published artifact and both `/api/v1/meta/*` endpoints actually emit, and it was the only channel never measured.

## ⚠️ The blast radius is wider than `record:alert`, in both polarities

Measured on the broken tree, through the real `SchemaRenderer`, with a non-matching row:

| node | key | expected | measured before fix |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `element:text` | `properties.visibleWhen` | hidden | **shown** (fail-OPEN) |
| `page:card` | `properties.visible` | hidden | **shown** (fail-OPEN) |
| `element:text` | `properties.hidden` | shown | **hidden** (fail-CLOSED — the node vanishes) |

The two HIDE legs return the fail-soft `true` un-negated, so a broken gate makes the node disappear entirely. A one-polarity fix or a one-polarity test would have covered half the defect.

## The fix

One guard, at the measured site, in both bag loops:

```ts
VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS.has(key) && isCelEnvelope(value) ? value : evaluate(value)
```

- `VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS` is built from the two arrays this file **already** declares (`VISIBILITY_SHOW_KEYS` / `VISIBILITY_HIDE_KEYS`), so it cannot drift from the chain `shouldHide` and `winningVisibilityKey` consult.
- `isCelEnvelope` matches the **`cel` dialect only**. `template` and dialect-less envelopes keep the legacy `${…}` behaviour byte-for-byte.
- Non-predicate bag keys keep the flattening they have always had.
- All six keys are stripped by the metadata destructure before `createElement`, so no object value can reach the DOM through this.
- ⛔ The normalizer is **not** touched. No compensating `??` alias, no widened parse anywhere.

Half 2: `record:alert`'s `visible` input declaration, `'string'` -> `['boolean', 'string', 'object']`.

## Contract readings — both verified at source (PM assumption E)

| side | reading |
|:--|:--|
| objectui registration | `{ name: 'visible', type: 'string' }` — `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` |
| renderer docblock | `visible?: string \| { dialect, source } \| boolean` — `record-alert.tsx` |
| `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0**, `ComponentPropsMap['record:alert'].visible` | `boolean \| string \| { dialect: 'cel'\|'cron'\|'template', source?, ast?, meta? }` |

Triage's reading is correct and the narrower contract is objectui's. Per `ComponentInput.type`'s own rule — "declare only arms the contract accepts **and** the renderer resolves" — the arm is declared in the same change that makes it reachable.

⚠️ **Bonus falsification:** the registration's own inline comment asserted 「`ComponentPropsMap` carries no `record:alert` entry at rc.6」. That row **does** exist in the installed 17.4.0. The stale clause is corrected in place (comment only, no behaviour).

⛔ `@objectstack/spec` is **not** touched. No cross-repo change is implied: the spec was already correct, as triage ruled.

## Acceptance — a render-level test, plus the ablation

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-alert.celEnvelope.test.tsx` mounts the **real** `record:alert` renderer through the real `SchemaRenderer`, with `visible` authored as `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'has(record.duplicate_status) && record.duplicate_status == "confirmed"' }` — the card's predicate verbatim — and asserts on **what a user sees**:

- **group A (controls)** — the harness paints the banner, and this exact channel can hide it. Without these, a `false` verdict would read "never rendered": this renderer has four `return null` paths.
- **group B** — **shown on the confirmed row, HIDDEN on `suspected` and on `null`**, plus a row with the field **absent entirely** (also hidden — which is what `has()` is for).
- **group C (the card's own ablation, pinned as the other arm)** — the bare non-envelope string gates correctly too, and the two arms now **agree on every row**. The inversion the card measured is gone. Both arms are pinned so a regression cannot pass by repairing one.

⚠️ The fail-soft default is what makes this invisible, so every assertion is on the **hidden** case; a shown-only suite cannot fail on this defect.

`packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.predicateEnvelopeConfigBag.test.tsx` pins the fix site itself: all six chain keys, both polarities, plus the three no-op claims (template envelope unchanged, non-predicate key unchanged, shallow-array pass-through).

### Ablation — the guard is load-bearing

Mutated on disk (guard short-circuited to `false`), proven landed (injected-marker count 1; blob `92bd0fd4` != `HEAD` `9cde7019`), run, then restored (blob back to `9cde7019`, `git diff HEAD` empty):

```
ABLATED:  Tests 10 failed | 6 passed (16)   <- incl. {onConfirmed:true, onSuspected:true, onUnset:true}, the card signature
RESTORED: Tests 16 passed (16)
```

Re-run at the shipped head `dcc4925`: guard blob `53a1c060`, mutated `126afb24`, restored `53a1c060`, `git diff HEAD` empty. These suites resolve through vitest's source aliases (the fault stack names `packages/core/src/…`), so no `dist/` leg is involved and the mutation demonstrably took effect.

## Gates

All at the shipped head `dcc4925`.

| command | exit |
|:--|:--|
| `vitest run --project unit --project dom --project dom-heavy packages/react/src/ packages/plugin-detail/src/ apps/console/src/__tests__/` | **0** — 242 files, 2461 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter "@object-ui/react^..." --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build` | **0** (12 projects) |
| `pnpm --filter "@object-ui/console^..." build` | **0** (35 projects) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` | **0** (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) |
| `node scripts/check-sdui-registration-pins.mjs` | **0** (16 registrations, 518 chunks weighed — needed the console build above; without it the gate exits 2 = measured nothing) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | **0** (7292 files) |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` | **0** |
| `eslint <the 5 changed files> --format json` | **0** — 0 errors, 47 warnings, **all pre-existing**: every warning line is outside the diff hunks and the `as any` count is unchanged (8 -> 8 in `SchemaRenderer.tsx`, 0 -> 0 in `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`) |

### Two gates that did real work, and what they cost

- **`registry-inputs-spec-parity`** refused the new `object` arm until `record:alert.visible` had a MEMBER PIN under objectui#8068. Registered, naming the render-level suite this PR adds. (198 tests green.)
- **`configBag.pin`** (objectui#6761) caught `isCelEnvelope` re-spelling the one config-bag predicate. It now ASKS `isConfigBag` instead — a third read of the one answer, not a fourth spelling. ⚠️ That gate lives in the `unit` project; a `--project dom --project dom-heavy` run alone does not see it.

**Declared narrowing.** The behaviour change is observable only by metadata carrying a `{dialect:'cel'}` envelope on one of six visibility keys at the top level of a `properties` / `props` bag. A scan of `packages/**` + `apps/**` + `examples/**` finds that shape in **7 files, all inside the two owning packages**, and all seven are inside the 242-file run above. Every other shape is a no-op by construction, pinned by the three no-op cases. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` / full-farm run is CI's, not measured here.

⛔ **Not attempted:** the optional browser leg. The in-process render-level suite already exercises the whole renderer -> `toPredicateInput` -> `useCondition` -> `evaluateCondition` chain, which is the gap a normalizer unit test leaves; driving a live preview would add a reading of the same chain at much higher cost.

## Census — triage asked for the exposed set, and 18 is not it

The PM's **18** is the population that *calls* `toPredicateInput`. The population *exposed to the flattening* is a different set, and it splits by tier.

**Membership rule:** a predicate is exposed iff it reaches its consumer as a **top-level key of the node's own `properties` / `props` bag** — i.e. it passes through the shallow per-value loop. A predicate nested inside an array/object value, or sourced from object metadata rather than the node, is not.

**Tier 1 — `SchemaRenderer`'s node gate: every registered component type, not a subset.** The gate reads the post-hoist node, and the hoist copies every `properties.*` key onto it, so exposure is a property of the **key**, not of the component. Six keys, both polarities. Measured above on `element:text` and `page:card`, neither of which reads a predicate itself.

**Tier 2 — renderers that re-read a predicate from their own bag: 10 call sites across 6 files.**

| file | sites |
|:--|:--|
| `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx` | `visible` ⟵ **the measured one** |
| `components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx` | `visible` |
| `components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx` | `visible`, `disabled`, `enabled` |
| `components/src/renderers/action/action-group.tsx` | `visible` |
| `components/src/renderers/action/action-icon.tsx` | `visible`, `disabled`, `enabled` |
| `components/src/renderers/action/action-menu.tsx` | `visible` |

**Excluded, with the reason** (this is the half that narrows 18 down): `DeclaredActionsBar` and `record-quick-actions` read `action.*` from **object metadata**, never from a node bag — that is the card's *working* path. `action-group` / `action-menu`'s per-item legs and `RelatedList`'s toolbar button read an element of an **array**, which the shallow loop passes through. `ActionEngine` / `ActionRunner` / `approvalOverride` / `declaredPredicate` / `schema-validator` / `predicateInput` / `useExpression` / `expression(.zod)` are engine- and type-level and never see a `SchemaRenderer`.

**This PR fixes the whole class in one stroke, and that is not a widening** — the fault was one shared line, so there was no narrower repair available that would have fixed `record:alert` alone. The *enablement* keys (`disabled` / `disabledOn` / `enabled`) are **deliberately left out of the guard** and filed instead; see below.

## Out-of-scope findings (⛔ not fixed here)

1. **Enablement keys have the same defect and are not covered.** `disabled` / `disabledOn` / `enabled` are not in the visibility chain and route through `evaluateEnablementPredicate`; a `cel` envelope on them is flattened by the same loops. Left out per triage's 「fix the measured one … do not widen unbidden」.
2. **The `props` bag never drove the node gate at all** — pre-existing and unrelated to the envelope. Measured on the same tree: `props: { visible: false }` renders, `props: { hidden: true }` renders, while the `properties` spelling of either decides correctly. The hoist copies `properties` onto the node and nothing copies `props`.
3. Noted, not filed: `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate`'s unwrap returns the **raw CEL source text** for a `cel` envelope on any non-predicate key — useless in every direction (it is not a template, so it is emitted verbatim). Not touched here because changing `evaluate` itself is a core-wide blast radius.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么** — `SchemaRenderer` 在把节点 `properties` / `props` 逐值求值时,不再把 `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` 断言信封拍平成裸字符串;顺带把 `record:alert` 的 `visible` 声明从 `'string'` 拓成 `['boolean','string','object']`,与 spec 已声明的契约对齐。

**为什么改** — 这是一个**失败时敞开**的可见性门禁。作者写「满足条件才显示」的横幅,平台在每一行都显示它;真实浏览器实测 6/6 条线索全部误显。信封是唯一把断言路由到权威 CEL 引擎的标记,拍平后落到遗留 JS 引擎,`has()` 不存在 ⇒ 抛错 ⇒ fail-soft 判定为「显示」。⚠️ 反向的两个键(`hidden` / `hiddenOn`)则相反:整个节点直接消失。两种都与「作者本意如此」在屏幕上完全同形,用户永远发现不了。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** — 这是**行为变更**:此前从不生效的 CEL 信封门禁现在真的生效了,依赖它「不咬人」的元数据会看到节点被隐藏(或反向显示)。范围经实测收窄:只有把 `cel` 信封写在六个可见性键之一、且位于 `properties` / `props` 顶层的元数据会变;`template` 信封、无 dialect 信封、非断言键全部逐字节不变,已各自钉住。回滚成本低——改动是两处循环里的一个守卫加一个常量,`git revert` 即可,无数据迁移、无 API 变更。

**席位意见** — (待填)

**你要做的** — 这张卡按 `Clause-②: yes` 走席内契约复核:需要确认的是**声明拓宽**这一半(`record:alert.visible` 从一个 arm 变三个 arm),以及上面「风险与代价」里那条行为变更是否接受。另外请留意:卡片正文与分诊都把缺陷定位在 normalizer,**实测证伪**,真正的故障点在上游一层——复核时请按实测的故障点读,不要按卡片叙述读。
